submitter: bugs_open/257 round 3, RESUBMISSION after REVISE (corr 5de01fd3). ⚠ The decision was carried by `decided_by: "unreadable reviewer(s)"` — 8 of 12 seats returned an unparseable result and 4 abstained, so only 4 verdicts were readable: editquality OBJECT (3, all about the SKETCHES under-showing the code), reuse_agent APPROVE with 2, prior_art_librarian OBJECT (2), constitution and mission APPROVE. Every objection is answered below with a measurement or a real diff. The code is committed (d88afbf84, f18704b9c) and the migration APPLIED (763c8002f) — review here is after the fact by design (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2), and nothing in the objections asks for a revert.
rationale:
OWNER DECISION 4, 2026-09-04, verbatim: "the limits are set in each individuals config, sometimes it has been set in the wrong place and sometimes the agent reads the wrong place, please fix it properly." This is bugs_open/257 round 3, and unlike rounds 1 and 2 it is not about Go literals — every literal is already gone. It is about a precedence rule that reads two of the four places an operator can legitimately write a budget, in an order that puts the LEAST specific first.

THE CENSUS, and it is the whole case. [MEASURED 2026-09-04, live agent_definitions, 208 active non-snapshot agents, by recursive jsonb walk rather than a fixed-path query] 171 declarations of max_tokens in five shapes:
  .workflow.steps.<step>.config.ai_service.max_tokens       149 decls / 74 agents   canonical
  .max_tokens                            (agent, bare)       10 decls /  9 agents   READ FIRST
  .workflow.steps.<step>.config.max_tokens                    7 decls /  2 agents   READ BY NOBODY
  .ai_service.max_tokens                 (agent, service)     3 decls /  3 agents
  ...<nested loop step>.config.ai_service.max_tokens          2 decls /  1 agent
The recursive walk matters: a fixed-path census would have missed the nested pair, and round 2's lesson (LANDMINES, 2026-09-03) is that four successive censuses of this bug all missed feed_actions.go by grepping the interface instead of the concept.

FAILURE (1), SHADOWED. ExecuteLLMPromptAction reads agentConfig["max_tokens"] BEFORE the merged ai_service block. All ten agents carrying a bare root key declare 8000 on their single LLM step, in the canonical place, and are pinned to 500-2000 by the leftover: content-creator-{about,contact x2,cta,features,hero,hero-without-research,testimonials} 2000/1500, content_researcher 1500, simple-content-writer-with-approval 500. Nothing logs it. [MEASURED] none of the ten has ever appeared in llm_call_log, all-history, so this is a latent cap on unrun agents, NOT live damage — stated because the opposite claim would be the easy overstatement here.

FAILURE (2), UNREAD. Nothing looks at a step's bare key. site-adoption-agent's four steps each carry an ai_service block holding model/provider/api_key_env_var — which ARE read — with max_tokens as a SIBLING of that block: analyze_site 32000, derive_content_direction 6000, classify_archetype 4000, generate_design_intent 4000. [MEASURED, 14 days to 2026-09-04] 8 calls, every one at the root 16000. analyze_site asked for double and got half; the other three asked for less and got more, so this is a spend question as well as a capability one.

WHY THE SHAPE FOOLS EVERYONE, and why a reader is the fix rather than a refusal: the misplaced key sits one brace outside a block whose OTHER keys are read. There is no error, no warning, and the definition reads correctly to inspection. Refusing the bare spelling instead of reading it would convert today's seventeen misplaced declarations into seventeen unconfigured steps at the 2048 floor — which is exactly the failure bugs_open/205 counted (8 of 126 steps unconfigured, 64 truncations before anything said so).

THE FIX, IN TWO INDEPENDENT HALVES. (a) One ladder, most-specific-first, with the canonical ai_service spelling consulted before the bare one at each level: step_config.ai_service > step_config > workflow_step.ai_service > workflow_step > root.ai_service > root. Both intra-level orderings are UNOBSERVABLE on today's fleet — [MEASURED 2026-09-04] no agent declares both spellings at any one level, asserted as guard 3 of the migration — so this fixes the two failures without silently re-deciding anything an operator has already written. (b) A migration that MOVES the misplaced numbers into the canonical place. It invents no numbers. It is live the moment it applies and fixes both failures under the CURRENT binary, so neither half waits for the other.

BEHAVIOUR AT THE WIRE, enumerated. Ten agents' single LLM step: 500-2000 -> 8000 (its own declaration; zero traffic, so zero requests change today). site-adoption-agent: 16000 -> 32000/6000/4000/4000. Two of those four go DOWN, so headroom is stated rather than assumed — largest observed output per step in 14 days: analyze_site 843, derive_content_direction 4167, classify_archetype 1017, generate_design_intent 1493, zero truncations all-history. Tightest new ceiling carries 1.4x its observed maximum. Everything else in the fleet is unaffected: 149 canonical step declarations and 3 canonical root ones resolve to the same number under both the old rule and the ladder.

ONE ORDERING CONSTRAINT THAT GENUINELY EXISTS, and it is the reason a _HOLD file is in this plan rather than one migration. html-developer-chunked's three steps (12000/4000/8000) are the ONE place in the estate where the bare spelling is the only one that works: getMaxTokens (html_actions.go) reads config["max_tokens"] and never looks at the step's ai_service block. Moving those three today silently gives all three that function's hardcoded 16000 default. So migration 769 deliberately leaves them, and 770_HOLD moves them by hand once a chassis image carrying the ladder is live, with the merge-base check written into the file. Per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 §2, an ordering constraint must be real and named; this one is, and it is the only one — the rest of the change explicitly does NOT claim it could have been held back.

WHAT ELSE THE CENSUS FOUND AND THIS CHANGE DOES NOT TOUCH, so the council is not asked to approve silence. [MEASURED 2026-09-04] budget_tokens: ZERO declarations fleet-wide, so extended thinking has never been configured; the ladder covers the key anyway so the first operator to declare one is not caught by a second rule. temperature: 72 step-level declarations across 12 agents (fix-proposer 21, council-gate 17, feature-designer 10 ...) all asking for 0.0, and ai_actions.go reads only agentConfig["temperature"] — none of the 12 has a root temperature, so all 72 are dead config. It is NOT fixed here and must not be: anthropic.go:300 deliberately sends no temperature at all ("Claude Opus 4.7+ returns a 400 for any non-default temperature"), so honouring them would be a no-op on every one of these agents and a live behaviour change on any future non-Anthropic one. It is reported by the new detector instead. Separately: two ACTIVE agent_definitions rows both claim type content-creator-contact with different budgets, which is a SingleOwner-shaped finding for another lane.

WHY A DETECTOR IS PART OF THE FIX, not a nice-to-have. llm_budget_call_sites_test.go — this lane's own round-2 guard — states in its header that it cannot see this class: "Config that is declared and read by nobody... no Go test can see it." A Go test is package-scoped and offline from the fleet; the thing that catches the eighteenth misplaced declaration is a report joined against live agent_definitions, which is what cmd/config-key-audit exists for and why the owner put it in council scope on 2026-08-23.

CANDIDATE 2 IS RULED, NOT DODGED. The owner's decision 2 on 2026-09-04 was "leave it". This plan honours that as option (c) of the three the handoff offered — the two rules differ permanently and the difference is now written down as a contract, with a test pinning it (TestDirectCallerLadderStaysTwoLevels). What the two ladders now share is only the WALKER (how a number is read out of a map, and which types count as configured); the LEVEL LISTS stay separate and separately documented, because a direct caller genuinely has no agent-level config to consult. This is deliberately not the datahelpers extraction the handoff costed as option (b), and there is no import cycle in it: both readers are in package actions.

═══ ROUND 2 OF THIS SUBMISSION — WHAT THE COUNCIL ASKED, AND WHAT MEASURING IT FOUND ═══

OBJECTION (reuse_agent, medium; prior_art_librarian, medium — raised INDEPENDENTLY by two seats, which
is why it was measured rather than argued): does the existing token-pressure machinery
(104_REPORT_seat_token_pressure_v1.sh, doc_notes `fleet-step-token-pressure` / `council-seat-token-pressure`)
already cover this, so that the new report is a parallel detector beside a live one rather than a
different question? The seats were right to ask, and right that the first submission cited bugs_open/205
as prior measurement without establishing liveness or overlap.

MEASURED 2026-09-04, by reading both scheduled_tasks rows, not by reading the wrapper script:

  `fleet-step-token-pressure`   ENABLED, every 21600s, last completed 2026-09-03 13:38, 15 findings in
      its latest note. Its pre_query reads `llm_call_log` and NOTHING ELSE — the cap it reports is
      `DISTINCT ON (step_name) max_tokens` taken from the calls themselves. It has no join to
      agent_definitions at any point.
  `council-seat-token-pressure` ENABLED, every 21600s, last completed 2026-09-04 10:17. Its pre_query
      DOES read agent_definitions, on exactly ONE fixed path —
      `s.value->'config'->'ai_service'->>'max_tokens'` — and only `WHERE s.key LIKE 'review_%'`.

So there is no overlap, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of emphasis:

 (a) DIFFERENT QUESTION. Both measure what was SENT against what came back: n, p95, peak, truncations.
     Neither can say where the number came from, because the sent number is the only budget either one
     ever sees. `site-adoption-agent.analyze_site` asked for 32000 and sent 16000; the fleet report shows
     that step at healthy headroom against 16000, which is TRUE and misses the entire defect.
 (b) DIFFERENT POPULATION, TWICE OVER. The seat report is council seats only. The fleet report is keyed
     on calls, so a step that has never RUN is invisible to it — and none of the ten shadowed agents has
     ever appeared in llm_call_log, so the whole of failure (1) sits outside what it can observe. The
     same holds for bugs_open/205's shape: an unconfigured step is invisible there until it truncates,
     which is the event the report exists to prevent.
 (c) THE ADJACENT MECHANISM IS ITSELF A CONSUMER OF THIS DEFECT. `council-seat-token-pressure` looks up
     a seat's cap on one of the four placements. A seat whose budget were declared at the agent root, or
     in the bare spelling, would return no cap row and be silently DROPPED from the report — not flagged,
     absent. [MEASURED 2026-09-04] all 51 live `review_%` seats across six councils declare canonically
     today, so this is a latent fragility and NOT live damage; the honest claim is that the placement
     report is what would notice if it stopped being true. Per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 §3, that
     mechanism's owner is being told rather than merely measured: bugs_open/138's lane, in the bug file.
 (d) IT ALREADY WORKS AND IS NOT BEING DUPLICATED. Its latest note flags
     `suggest_related_pages@300 — n=217, p95 100.0%, peak 100.0%, truncated 40`. That is a real live
     defect — a 300-token budget declared correctly, in the canonical place, and simply too small. It is
     exactly what a runtime-pressure report is for and exactly what a placement report cannot see, and
     this change deliberately does not touch it.

OBJECTION (editquality, medium ×2 + low, all three about the SKETCHES). Correct, and the fault was the
submission's, not the code's. Migration 769's sketch showed only the agent-root move and not the
step-level one — which is the actively-firing half — and used `subConfigMap` and `workflowStepConfig`
without showing them defined. The edits below now carry the REAL diffs from the committed change,
including the full step-level jsonb rewrite and both helper definitions. Guard 3 is per-level in the
applied file: it aborts on both-spellings-at-one-level at the root AND at the step, as two separate
counts. The dry run (COMMIT replaced by ROLLBACK) executed all four guards, both UPDATEs and the verify
block before anything was applied — and caught a genuine defect in the step-level statement that no
sketch review would have: PostgreSQL binds subtraction tighter than `->`, so
`s.value->'config' - 'max_tokens'` parsed as `s.value -> ('config' - 'max_tokens')`.

OBJECTION (prior_art_librarian, low): "no check was run to confirm cmd/config-key-audit's existing files
implement the ladder-aware traversal the new file claims to reuse... a parity test asserts the two agree".
That sentence was in the first submission's sketch and it is now FALSE, so it is withdrawn rather than
defended: there is no parity test, because there is nothing to keep in parity. The detector calls
`actions.ResolveStepBudget` — production's own function, exported in the same commit — so the rule has
one implementation. What it borrows from the existing files is only their SHAPE (stdin export, findings
JSON, --report doc_notes row, exit 0/1/2), and `validation.WalkSteps` for the descent into loop
sub-workflows, which is the same call audit-default-shadowed-keys.sh's binary makes.

OBJECTION (reuse_agent, low): does an equivalent generic ladder-walk already exist? Checked:
`grep -rn "intFromConfig\|GetIntField\|ExtractNestedFieldInt"` returns `datahelpers.GetIntField`
(float64/int only, returns a bare int with a default) and `datahelpers.ExtractNestedFieldInt` (returns 0
for missing). Both collapse "the operator chose nothing" and "the operator chose 0" into one int, and
that distinction is the whole reason this walker returns (value, from, shadowed) — `max_tokens: 0` is a
hard 400 from Anthropic and must be treated as unset. `platform/aiservice/max_tokens.go` records the same
check being made, and reaching the same conclusion, when the seat asked it in August.

═══ WHAT CHANGED IN THE CODE SINCE THE FIRST SUBMISSION, unprompted by the council ═══

Writing the detector found a defect in the ladder commit that had already landed, and it is the most
useful thing in this round. The first cut reported "shadowed" whenever two levels declared different
numbers, and its FIRST RUN against the live fleet returned 18 findings, every one healthy: a root
`ai_service` default beaten by a step declaration is the DOCUMENTED overlay design
(resolveAIServiceConfig: "the root block is the fleet default, the current step's block overrides it
key-by-key"), and feed-triage does it on purpose — root 4000, steps 8000 and 8192. The identical
over-reporting was in the runtime Warn already committed in ai_actions.go, where it would have fired on
every call of 18 live steps. Both are removed. The finding kind that replaces it is AMBIGUOUS: one LEVEL
declaring both spellings with different numbers, which is the one state where the estate's two readers
send different numbers for the same step. Zero live instances, and it is also migration 769's guard 3.
Both non-findings are now pinned by name in the tests so they cannot come back.

plan.summary: REVISION of corr 5de01fd3 (REVISE, carried by 8 unreadable seats). Same change, unchanged in intent: one six-level token-budget ladder replacing an inverted two-arm read, the third reader aligned, 14 misplaced declarations migrated into the canonical place, and a fleet report for the class no Go test can see. What is new here is evidence rather than code: the two live token-pressure scheduled_tasks are read and shown to answer a different question over a different population; every sketch is now the real committed diff, including the step-level migration statements editquality could not verify; one false claim in the first submission is withdrawn; and one defect the detector found in the already-committed ladder — an override warning that would have fired on 18 healthy live steps — is corrected and pinned by test.

edits.rationale: The ladder and the contract that governs it, in the package's existing budget file rather than a new one. resolveBudgetKey returns the winning value, the NAME of the level it came from, and every other level that declares the key — the third return is what lets a caller say out loud that an operator's number was overridden, which is the fact that was missing for both live failures. numericConfigValue accepts int/int64/float64/json.Number: the reader it replaces in ai_actions.go was float64-ONLY, so a viper-decoded (YAML) budget was silently dropped there while platform/aiservice honoured it — two readers of one key disagreeing about what counts as configured is the drift class this bug is about, and they now agree. intFromConfig keeps its own two-level list and a comment stating that the difference from the canonical ladder is permanent and ruled (candidate 2, option (c)). REVISION: editquality objected that budgetLevelsForStep used subConfigMap without it being defined anywhere in the plan. It is defined in this same file and the diff below now shows it, together with numericConfigValue and the exported ResolveStepBudget the detector calls. Also changed since the first submission: resolveBudgetKey now counts a level as shadowing ONLY when it declares a DIFFERENT number, because a top-level step's config reaches the ladder at two rungs and the first version would have called 149 healthy live steps shadowed.

The defect itself. The block being deleted is the whole of failure (1) and (2): agentConfig["max_tokens"] first, merged ai_service second, step-level bare key never. budget_tokens moves to the same ladder — [MEASURED] zero live declarations, so that arm changes nothing today and exists so a second precedence rule cannot appear later. The new Info log names WHICH level supplied the number, and a Warn fires when more than one level declares it: round 3 was diagnosed by re-deriving that by hand against a jsonb census, and nobody should have to do that twice. workflowStepConfig is factored out of resolveAIServiceConfig so the ai_service overlay and the budget ladder reach the step through ONE traversal rather than two hand-written descents into the same four-deep path (bugs_open/144's shape). REVISION: editquality objected (low) that workflowStepConfig's extraction from resolveAIServiceConfig was asserted in prose and not shown. The diff below carries both halves — the new function and the four nested type assertions it replaces inside resolveAIServiceConfig. The override Warn shown in the first submission is GONE, for the reason in the rationale: it would have fired on every call of 18 healthy live steps.

The third reader, and the one that creates the plan's only ordering constraint. It reads the BARE key and ignores the step's ai_service block entirely — so html-developer-chunked's three steps work today only because they happen to be written the way this one function reads, and any operator moving them to the canonical place would silently get its hardcoded 16000. Reading both spellings in the same order as every other call site is precisely what makes migration 770 safe, and it is why 770 is HELD rather than folded into 769. No behaviour change today: [MEASURED] all three declarations are bare, so the ladder resolves the same numbers.

The two central cases are built from the shapes that were ACTUALLY WRONG on the live fleet on 2026-09-04, not invented ones, so they are regression tests rather than restatements of the code. MUTATION-PROVEN, both directions: restoring the old level order fails TestLiveShadowedRootKeyNoLongerCapsItsOwnStep with 'the step declared 8000 in the canonical place and resolved to 2000 from "root"'; deleting the two bare-key levels fails all four sub-cases of TestLiveMisplacedStepKeyIsNowRead with 'the bare spelling is unread again'. TestWorkflowStepConfigFindsOnlyATopLevelStep asserts the traversal returns nil for a synthesised loop-body step name — a silent non-nil there would feed the ladder a DIFFERENT step's config, which reads as working. The sibling guard (llm_budget_call_sites_test.go) is untouched and still passes: 10 model call sites, 7 budget-key writes.

The configuration half, and the half that is live without a roll. It MOVES 14 declarations (10 agent-level, 4 site-adoption-agent step-level) into the canonical ai_service block; it invents no numbers. Three DO/RAISE guards, not SELECTs — ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set, so a verify made of SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT (LANDMINES). Guard 1 and 2 abort if the census has moved (a census goes stale BY ADDITION and reads as current for ever — owner ruling 2026-08-22); guard 3 aborts if any agent declares BOTH spellings at one level, which is the only shape in which this migration could destroy an operator's number. The verify asserts the moved values ARE 32000/6000/4000/4000 and that root ai_service declarations went 3 -> 13, so a move that lost a value cannot pass; and it asserts html-developer-chunked still has its 3, because a migration that quietly took those too would look identical to this one succeeding. REVISION, answering editquality's medium objection directly: the first sketch showed only the agent-root move and guard 3's root half, so the step-level move — the actively-firing half — was unverifiable. The applied statements are below in full, including the snapshot_agent block, the jsonb_object_agg that rebuilds workflow.steps key-by-key (the only way to address a varying step name in one statement), and the parenthesisation the ROLLBACK dry run forced. Guard 3 is TWO counts in the applied file, root and step, not one. APPLIED and recorded 2026-09-04; verified after: zero bare root declarations (was 10), 13 canonical root (was 3), 153 canonical step (was 149), site-adoption-agent now sending 32000/6000/4000/4000.
edits.sketch:
+    FROM agent_definitions a, LATERAL jsonb_each(COALESCE(a.default_config->'workflow'->'steps','{}'::jsonb)) s
+   WHERE a.is_active AND COALESCE(a.is_snapshot,false)=false AND a.deleted_at IS NULL
+     AND jsonb_typeof(a.default_config->'workflow'->'steps')='object'
+     AND s.value->'config' ? 'max_tokens' AND s.value->'config'->'ai_service' ? 'max_tokens';
+  IF n > 0 THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION '769 ABORT: % steps declare max_tokens at BOTH step spellings; moving would clobber one.', n;
+  END IF;
+END $$;
+
+-- Snapshot every agent this file rewrites, before it rewrites it. House convention
+-- for any migration touching agent_definitions, and the practical rollback path: the
+-- ROLLBACK file restores the values, these rows restore the whole definition if the
+-- jsonb surgery below turns out to have taken something with it.
+DO $$
+DECLARE t text;
+BEGIN
+  FOR t IN
+    SELECT DISTINCT type FROM agent_definitions
+     WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL
+       AND (default_config ? 'max_tokens' OR type = 'site-adoption-agent')
+  LOOP
+    PERFORM snapshot_agent(t, '769_token_budgets_move_to_the_one_place_every_reader_looks.sql: pre-update');
+  END LOOP;
+END $$;
+
+-- ── (1) the agent-level bare key moves into the agent's ai_service block ──────────────────────
+-- Every one of the ten already HAS a root ai_service block (checked 2026-09-04), so this adds a
+-- key to an existing object rather than creating one; jsonb_set with create_if_missing does both.
+UPDATE agent_definitions
+   SET default_config =
+         (default_config - 'max_tokens')
+         || jsonb_build_object('ai_service',
+              COALESCE(default_config->'ai_service','{}'::jsonb)
+              || jsonb_build_object('max_tokens', default_config->'max_tokens')),
+       updated_at = now()
+ WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL
+   AND default_config ? 'max_tokens';
+
+-- ── (2) site-adoption-agent's four step-level bare keys move into each step's ai_service ──────
+-- Named by agent rather than applied to all 7, because html-developer-chunked's three must NOT
+-- move yet (see the header). Rebuilding the steps object key-by-key is the only way to address a
+-- varying step name in one statement.
+UPDATE agent_definitions a
+   SET default_config = jsonb_set(a.default_config, '{workflow,steps}', (
+         SELECT jsonb_object_agg(s.key,
+                  CASE WHEN s.value->'config' ? 'max_tokens'
+                       -- ⚠ ((s.value->'config') - 'max_tokens'), not s.value->'config' - 'max_tokens':
+                       -- PostgreSQL binds subtraction TIGHTER than ->, so the unparenthesised form
+                       -- parses as s.value -> ('config' - 'max_tokens') and fails with
+                       -- "operator is not unique: unknown - unknown". Caught by executing this file
+                       -- with COMMIT replaced by ROLLBACK before applying it.
+                       THEN jsonb_set(s.value, '{config}',
+                              ((s.value->'config') - 'max_tokens')
+                              || jsonb_build_object('ai_service',
+                                   COALESCE(s.value->'config'->'ai_service','{}'::jsonb)
+                                   || jsonb_build_object('max_tokens', s.value->'config'->'max_tokens')))
+                       ELSE s.value END)
+           FROM jsonb_each(a.default_config->'workflow'->'steps') s)),
+       updated_at = now()
+ WHERE a.type = 'site-adoption-agent'
+   AND a.is_active AND COALESCE(a.is_snapshot,false)=false AND a.deleted_at IS NULL;
+
+-- ── VERIFY: a DO block, not a SELECT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set, so a verify block made of SELECTs cannot stop the
+-- COMMIT (LANDMINES.md). These RAISE.
+DO $$
+DECLARE bare_root int; bare_step int; moved int;
+BEGIN
+  SELECT count(*) INTO bare_root FROM agent_definitions
+   WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL
+     AND default_config ? 'max_tokens';
+  IF bare_root <> 0 THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION '769 VERIFY FAILED: % agents still carry a bare root max_tokens', bare_root;

edits.rationale: The three declarations with the real ordering constraint, held out of the runner and applied by hand once the ladder is live. _HOLD is the estate's own idiom for exactly this (SIDECAR_RE excludes it from the runner while still listing it). The apply condition is written into the file as a CHECK, not a judgement: read the chassis pod's build provenance line and run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <round-3 commit> <that sha>`, with the note that an empty provenance grep means 'not in range' because it is a STARTUP line, not 'unstamped'. Its ROLLBACK exists for the case that matters — if the ladder is rolled back after 770 has applied, the budgets inside ai_service become invisible to the old getMaxTokens and all three steps silently take 16000, so restoring the bare spelling is what makes them readable again.

edits.rationale: The detector, and the reason it belongs HERE rather than in a Go test: this class is invisible to a package-scoped offline test by construction, and llm_budget_call_sites_test.go says so in its own header ('config that is declared and read by nobody... no Go test can see it'). It joins the compiled precedence rule against live agent_definitions and reports, per LLM step: every level that declares a budget, which one WINS under the shipped ladder, and three finding kinds — `shadowed` (a declaration that loses to a less specific one; impossible after this change and watched anyway, because the ladder is what could regress), `non_canonical` (declared outside ai_service — honoured, but the placement that started this), and `unconfigured` (an LLM step with no budget at any level, i.e. bugs_open/205's shape, which nothing currently counts). VACUITY: refuses to report over an export containing zero LLM steps or zero budget declarations — 'the check could not run' must never read as 'the check passed' (016b §9). Needs a new root-config projection in the stdin export, added the way AgentPromptTemplate was (json.RawMessage, so an absent projection is distinguishable from a null) and REFUSED if missing, because without the agent's root config every finding's precedence verdict would be silently wrong. REVISION: the first submission's sketch claimed 'a parity test asserts the two agree'. That is withdrawn as false — there is no parity test because there is nothing to keep in parity: the mode calls actions.ResolveStepBudget, production's own exported function. And the overlap question both seats raised is answered in the rationale by reading the two live scheduled_tasks rows: fleet-step-token-pressure joins nothing but llm_call_log, council-seat-token-pressure reads ONE of the four placements and only for review_% seats, and neither can see a declaration that never reaches the wire or a step that has never run. Also changed since the first submission: the 'shadowed' finding kind is replaced by 'ambiguous', after the first live run returned 18 findings that were all healthy.
edits.sketch:
+type budgetFinding struct {
+	Agent string `json:"agent"`
+	Path  string `json:"path"`
+	Kind  string `json:"kind"` // shadowed | non_canonical | unconfigured
+	Effective int `json:"effective"`
+	From  string `json:"from"`

edits.rationale: The wrapper, identical in shape to audit-default-shadowed-keys.sh and for the same reason its comment gives: WalkSteps in the Go binary descends into loop sub-workflows itself, so the SQL export must not try to (bugs_open/144). This export adds the agent's root config to the projection the other wrappers use, because the two lowest levels of the ladder live there and a report without them would grade every step against a truncated rule. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could-not-determine, matching the family. Prints the DECLARED-versus-EFFECTIVE table an operator can act on, grouped by kind, with the verdict taken from the binary rather than re-derived in the shell — the mistake audit-default-shadowed-keys.sh documents having made.

+WORKFLOWS_JSON="$(psql_q "

+WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false) = false AND is_active

+FINDINGS_JSON="$(printf '%s' "$WORKFLOWS_JSON" | (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --budget-placement) 2>"$ERR")"

grounded_in: platform/orchestration/actions/ai_actions.go (before this change) — `if maxTokens, ok = agentConfig["max_tokens"].(float64); ok { options["max_tokens"] = int(maxTokens) } else if maxTokens, ok = aiServiceConfig["max_tokens"].(float64); ok {...}` — the two arms, in that order. The AGENT's bare key beats every step-level declaration, and no arm reads a step's bare key.

platform/orchestration/actions/llm_options.go — "That function's outer key is `agentConfig` ... the AGENT's whole default config, not the step's. So its rule is *agent-level beats ai_service*" — the difference was already recorded by the council's llm_reliability seat on 2026-08-10 as a documentation correction; nobody had yet asked whether agent-level SHOULD beat step-level.

platform/orchestration/actions/llm_budget_call_sites_test.go — "WHAT THIS AUDIT CANNOT SEE ... Config that is declared and read by nobody. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] four `site-adoption-agent` steps declare a top-level `config.max_tokens` (32000/4000/6000/4000) and every one of them runs at the root 16000, because no reader looks there. That is the same defect from the config end, and no Go test can see it." — this change is that sentence being answered.

platform/orchestration/actions/html_actions.go — `maxTokens := getMaxTokens(config, 16000)` then `llmParams.StepConfig.Config = map[string]interface{}{"ai_service": map[string]interface{}{... "max_tokens": maxTokens}}` — the third reader, which reads the bare key and synthesises an ai_service block around it.

platform/aiservice/anthropic.go:300-303 — "// Temperature is intentionally NOT sent to Anthropic. // Claude Opus 4.7+ returns a 400 for any non-default temperature" — the reason the 72 dead step-level temperature declarations are reported rather than honoured.

platform/aiservice/max_tokens.go — "A value must be > 0. Zero is not 'no budget', it is a 400 from Anthropic, so it is treated as unset ... (This matches `llmOptionsFromConfig`'s `intFromConfig`, deliberately: two readers of one key that disagree about what counts as configured is the drift class bugs_open/257 §3 is about.)" — the rule numericConfigValue is written to match, now including the int64/json.Number arms that ai_actions.go lacked.
